title: I Took the Aerial-Hoop Checkout to the Coach Who Left My Numbered Span

parts.text: I stepped into bay two at 7:07 p.m. and coach Mira was already using my numbered span. The board said: FORTY MINUTES. SPANS STAY WITH THE BOOKING. I was twenty-four, studio lead, holding a clipboard that listed our invert. Mira shrugged. "Coaches keep the hoop." I photographed the board, the booking, and her tape on my span. Then I asked for the hoop checkout. At 7:15 the aerial desk pinged why Mira's tape sat on our span. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The aerial desk can see Mira's tape in bay two during our invert.

social.video_title: She left her tape on my numbered aerial hoop — Part 1/2
social.description: Aerial hoop, a coach on my span, a forty-minute clock she posted. I logged the tape. Would you have asked for the hoop checkout?

parts.text: Mira called it spins until the desk asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the span still. The span went back to my numbered bag. Mira ran a slot of their own and told the next coach atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: COACHES DO NOT KEEP THE HOOP. I keep our invert on a labeled card. Mira brown-bags her tape. The bay finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Coaches do not keep the hoop — Part 2/2
social.description: Hoop checkout, numbered span, and a second line on the board. Were spins ever our invert?
